subject: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medspect.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Sarah — appreciate you walking us through the workflow and the regulatory constraints. Quick recap and a concrete proposal so we can align legal and engineering: 

1) What we heard you need
- No raw transcript storage beyond live inference for clinician-facing notes (PII-sensitive).
- Short-term KV caching for session continuity (speech->NLP context) but limited to a small window.
- Audit logs for access events kept for compliance (role-based, redacted where possible).
- Data residency: US-only region for both cache and audit logs.

2) What Redwood can offer today (proposal summary)
- Live inference only for model inputs: model does not persist full transcripts after inference unless explicitly requested.
- Configurable KV cache window: default 1 hour, option to shorten to 30 minutes for an additional control.
- Audit log retention: 180 days by default; we can offer a negotiated 90-day window for MedSpect with scoped exports.
- Residency: host cache and logs in our US-operated region; SOC2 evidence and KMS integrations available.

3) Compromise proposal (to unblock procurement/legal)
- 0-persistence for model inputs by default (no long-term transcript storage).
- Allow a 24-hour scoped, encrypted KV cache for session recovery when clinicians explicitly opt-in; automatic purge after window.
- Audit logs retained 90 days with redaction of PII fields; full logs available under Data Subject Request process.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short proposal PDF with the exact TTLs and technical controls (attached).
- Ben (cc) will work with engineering on the implementation checklist and timing.
- If this looks ok, we can put together a procurement term sheet and limited pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate the purge mechanics.

Attachments: redwood-ttl-compromise-proposal.pdf (proposal + config), medspect-data-specs.xlsx (your sample fields mapped)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medspect.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

> 0-persistence for model inputs by default (no long-term transcript storage).

This is critical. We cannot have transcripts persisted in any form unless we trigger an explicit retention action (e.g., clinician marks note for record).

> Allow a 24-hour scoped, encrypted KV cache for session recovery when clinicians explicitly opt-in; automatic purge after window.

24 hours is more than our security team is comfortable with for free-text clinician notes. Can you quantify what the tradeoffs are between 1 hour vs 24 hours for session recovery? Is the session continuity user-facing (i.e., will clinicians notice dropped context if we shorten to 1 hour)?

> Audit logs retained 90 days with redaction of PII fields

We need to see the PII redaction approach — if redaction is pattern-based only, our compliance team will push back.

We’re looping in legal (legal@medspect.com) for procurement language. Would appreciate Ben being on the engineering itemization.

—Sarah
Director of Product, MedSpect

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medspect.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise

Kim — I’ll take point on the engineering breakdown. A couple quick notes for legal/ops: 

- Technical tradeoff (1h vs 24h): most drop-off in context happens when prompts exceed ~1k tokens worth of incremental conversation; for short clinician interactions (one-off note entry) a 1-hour window preserves continuity in practice. 24h is mainly for workflows where clinicians resume lengthy sessions across a day.
- Implementation option: scoped cache keys per-session + automatic TTL enforcement at the storage layer (no manual deletion by app code). We can expose a config flag in the route: cache_ttl_seconds and a boolean require_clinician_consent.
- Redaction approach: we can provide two modes — automated pattern redaction (fast) and a stricter PII-hashing mode where sensitive fields (SSNs, MRNs) are hashed server-side before being logged; hashing prevents retrieval of original values while still allowing counts/metrics.

I’ll map these into the attached RFC for the pilot. Estimated engineering lift for a limited pilot (US region, 1-hour ttl default, 90-day audit retention, PII-hash opt-in) is ~2 sprints (4 weeks) with a small infra change + config UI for the consent toggle.

—Ben
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medspect.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, legal@medspect.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise

Thanks Ben — and Sarah, attached is the PDF with the exact values and the minimal pilot scope. Highlights: 

- Pilot configuration (2 weeks): cache_ttl_seconds = 3600 (1 hour), clinician_consent = on, cache_encryption = AES-256, auto_purge = true.
- Pilot acceptance criteria: no persisted transcript artifacts in the long-term store, automated purge logs available, redaction/hash verification run against sample dataset you provided.
- Legal items to include in term sheet: explicit call-out to 0-persistence for model inputs unless clinician triggers retention; data residency clause (US-only); SLA on purge completion (within 30 minutes of TTL expiry).

Doc links: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/sales/shared/medspect-ttl-proposal (contains the attached PDF and the mapping sheet).

If legal signs off on the pilot term sheet, we can schedule kickoff next Monday June 15. If you’d like, Ben and I can join a short legal Q&A to walk the engineering pieces.

Attachments: redwood-ttl-compromise-proposal.pdf, medspect-data-specs.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@medspect.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, legal@medspect.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: MedSpect persistence scope & proposed compromise

Appreciate the fast follow-up and the RFC, Kimberly and Ben. We’ve reviewed the proposal with security and legal; high-level feedback: 

- 1-hour TTL with clinician opt-in is acceptable for the pilot.
- We need the PII-hashing workflow documented (how keys are managed, re-identification risk). Please provide the design notes before kickoff.
- Add a clause that audit-log exports are only provided under a signed DPA-approved process; no ad-hoc raw exports.

I asked legal to draft a short pilot addendum and will circulate once ready. Please hold June 15 for the kickoff window; we’ll confirm by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
Sarah
